title: Template and Proxy (2021)
headline: Two supporting lemmas are false as stated, and two applications hold only under an assumption the paper does not state. The main theorem (Theorem 1) was not examined.

claims.label: Lemma 4
claims.gist: Serial shares are monotone in every user's demand.
claims.statement: On every tree network, each user's serial cost share is non-decreasing in every other user's demand.
claims.quantifiers: for every tree network and every demand profile

result.summary: A three-user path where one user's share falls when another's demand rises.
result.witness: On a path with three users and concave edge costs, raising the middle user's demand lowers the first user's share. The costs and both demand profiles are listed in the evidence package.
result.tested: All paths and stars with up to four users, integer demands up to five, exact rational arithmetic.
not_claimed: Theorem 1 is not claimed to be false; its proof uses Lemma 4 only for linear costs, where the lemma holds.
The lemma is not claimed to fail for linear edge costs.

vor_check.detail: Statement and definitions checked on rendered pages; the proof compared in extracted text only.

checks.detail: A separate AI session, not given the earlier result, rebuilt the example.
The researcher recomputed both cost shares with separately written code.

reproduction.detail: The evidence package reruns with one command (Python 3.12, standard library only).

claims.novelty: No earlier report found in the searched literature.

claims.label: Lemma 12
claims.gist: Merging two users never raises their combined share.
claims.statement: If two users on the same branch are merged into one user with their combined demand, their total cost share does not increase.
claims.quantifiers: for every pair of users on a branch

result.summary: Merging two users on a four-edge branch raises their combined share.
result.witness: On a branch with four edges, merging the two outermost users raises their combined share from 7 to 8 because the merged demand crosses a cost breakpoint.
result.tested: All branches with up to five edges and two to four users.
not_claimed: The lemma is not claimed to fail when the cost function has no breakpoints.

vor_check.detail: Statement and definitions checked on rendered pages; the proof compared in extracted text only.

checks.detail: A separate AI session, given the earlier result, checked the example against the printed definitions.
The researcher verified both totals by hand.

reproduction.detail: The evidence package reruns with one command (Python 3.12, standard library only).

claims.novelty: No earlier report found in the searched literature.

claims.label: Application to airport games (Section 6.1)
claims.gist: The serial rule coincides with the nucleolus in airport games.
claims.statement: In every airport game, the serial cost-sharing rule selects the nucleolus.
conditions: airport game: costs nested along a single runway

result.summary: Holds only when no two planes have equal runway needs; the paper does not say so.
result.witness: With two planes that need the same runway length, the serial rule and the nucleolus split their segment differently. With distinct needs, no counterexample exists in the cases checked.
result.tested: All airport games with up to six planes and integer runway lengths up to five.
not_claimed: The application is not claimed to fail when runway needs are distinct.
result.repair_note: Requiring distinct runway needs restores the application in all cases checked.

vor_check.detail: Statement and definitions checked on rendered pages; the proof compared in extracted text only.

checks.detail: The researcher computed both allocations with separate code.
A separate AI session confirmed the example.

reproduction.detail: The evidence package reruns with one command (Python 3.12, standard library only).

claims.novelty: No earlier report found in the searched literature.

claims.label: Application to irrigation networks (Section 6.2)
claims.gist: The serial rule is consistent on irrigation networks.
claims.statement: On irrigation networks, the serial rule is consistent: removing a user and their share leaves the others' shares unchanged.
conditions: irrigation network: a rooted tree with costs on edges

result.summary: Consistency needs every edge cost to be strictly positive; zero-cost edges break it.
result.witness: A four-user network with one zero-cost edge, where removing a leaf user changes another user's share.
result.tested: Networks with up to five users, with and without zero-cost edges.
not_claimed: The application is not claimed to fail when every edge cost is positive.
result.repair_note: Requiring strictly positive edge costs restores consistency in all cases checked.
